_comment: Per-artwork artist corrections, keyed by objectKey (folder/filename, NFC-normalised). Applied by build-data.mjs BEFORE the artists-db lookup, so a corrected name still picks up curated movement/nationality/dates. The lookup is by exact name or alias only, so a qualified name such as "Imitator of Thomas Gainsborough" stays its own artist instead of resolving to the painter it names. A null value clears the artist so the work falls into the anonymous bucket - used when the Commons `artist` field names only the uploader/photographer of the reproduction and the underlying creator is genuinely unrecorded. Never guess an attribution to fill a hole: every entry below cites the evidence it came from, the holding institution's own record wherever one exists. Regenerate data with `pnpm assets:build-data` after editing.

Commons category "Marriage at Cana (Paulo Veronese)" + PD-Art (Yorck Project); only the reproducing photographer was unknown.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Michelangelo_libyan: File description: "MICHELANGELO Buonarroti Study for the Libyan Sibyl"; Commons category "Drawings by Michelangelo Buonarroti in the Metropolitan Museum of Art".
_why.collection-of-beauty/El_Tres_de_Mayo,_by: Commons `artist` field is the derivative-work credit block verbatim: "El_Tres_de_Mayo,_by_Francisco_de_Goya,_from_Prado_in_Google_Earth.jpg : Francisco de Goya derivative work: Papa Lima Whiskey 2". "Papa Lima Whiskey 2" is the Commons user who cropped the black margin; the credit line confirms it ("This file was derived from: El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg"). The loose alias matcher used to rescue this by hitting "Goya" as a bare substring, and the record still resolves today only through the stale `artist_info` snapshot baked into the sidecar - a re-fetch under the strict matcher drops both, leaving the whole credit block as the artist name.
_why.collection-of-beauty/溥僩丙子夏日寫生.jpg: The catalogue read the painter's name as 'Pu Xuan'; the character is 僩 (xiàn). The inscription reads 丙子夏日為 鬟雪女史 雅屬 毅齋溥僩 寫生, signed with his courtesy name Yizhai, matching the signature on Bonhams lot 'Pu Xian (1901-1966), Flowers and Rocks, 1939' (https://www.bonhams.com/auction/26180/lot/45/pu-xian-1901-1966-flowers-and-rocks-1939/). Commons also gives 'Pu Xian' (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E6%BA%A5%E5%83%A9%E4%B8%99%E5%AD%90%E5%A4%8F%E6%97%A5%E5%AF%AB%E7%94%9F.jpg).
_why.collection-of-beauty/Портрет_художника_Ф: Tretyakov Gallery magazine illustration catalogue (https://www.tg-m.ru/catalog/artists/2446, ID 17657): 'Горавский Аполлинарий — Портрет художника Ф.А. Бруни, 1871, холст, масло, 105,4 × 78,5, ГТГ'. The accompanying article by Lyudmila Markina, 'Федор Бруни. Начало династии', Tretyakov Gallery Magazine #1 2018 (58) (https://www.tg-m.ru/articles/1-2018-58/fedor-bruni-nachalo-dinastii) quotes Goravsky's 1871 letters to Pavel Tretyakov about painting the commission and records the signature on the chair arm 'А. Горавскш 20 III 1871'. The live 'Andrey Denyer' came from the Commons file Bruni_FA.jpg, a Denyer photograph. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. Read both tg-m.ru pages; viewed the catalogued image: an oil painting of Bruni seated in a carved red armchair holding a porte-crayon, with a Cyrillic signature on the chair arm at lower left, matching the letter's description (seated, hands lowered, holding a pencil, black velvet coat). Image 753x1024 (0.735) matches 78.5/105.4 (0.745).
_why.collection-of-beauty/Allee_de_chataignie: Paris Musées / Petit Palais record PPP693 (https://www.parismuseescollections.paris.fr/en/node/227063): creator 'Sisley, Alfred (Paris, 30-10-1839 - Moret-sur-Loing, 22-01-1899), peintre'; signed lower left 'Sisley 65'. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. Read the record page and matched the museum image to the catalogued file; 'Alfred Sisley' is the spelling the catalogue already uses for this artist.
_why.collection-of-beauty/George_Frederic_Wat: National Portrait Gallery, London, NPG 5223 (https://www.npg.org.uk/collections/search/portrait/mw06625/George-Frederic-Watts): George Frederic Watts by Louis Reid Deuchars, after a photograph by George Andrews, oil on canvas, 1899, 917 x 715 mm, signed and dated lower right 'Louis R Deuchars 99', purchased 1978; shows Watts in a long red gown seated in an alcove at Limnerslease below a Della Robbia majolica of the Virgin and Child. Commons file page (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:George_Frederic_Watts_by_George_Andrews.jpg) has author = Creator:Louis Deuchars, accession NPG 5223, wikidata Q28050807; Wikidata SPARQL for P217 'NPG 5223' returns Q28050807 with P18 = this exact file. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. Read Commons wikitext and ran the Wikidata query myself; npg.org.uk blocks direct fetches (Cloudflare 403), so the NPG attribution text was read via two web searches of the indexed NPG pages, both naming Louis Reid Deuchars. Viewed the catalogued image: red robe, skullcap, Della Robbia roundel, orange trees, matching NPG's description; image 2400x3095 (0.78) matches 715/917 (0.78). Note: NPG and Wikidata date the work 1899; the live year 1897 (from the Commons batch boilerplate) looks wrong but is not changed here.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Cezanne_Ambroise_Vo: Paris Musées / Petit Palais, inventory PPP2100, 'Portrait d'Ambroise Vollard', author 'Cézanne, Paul (Aix-en-Provence, 19-01-1839 - Aix-en-Provence, 22-10-1906), peintre', dated 'En 1899', oil on canvas, 101 x 81 cm (https://www.parismuseescollections.paris.fr/fr/petit-palais/oeuvres/portrait-d-ambroise-vollard). The Commons file 'Cezanne Ambroise Vollard.jpg' cites that exact URL as its source. Its description reads 'Portrait of Ambroise Vollard (1899). Petit Palais, Paris', in category 'Ambroise Vollard (Paul Cézanne - Petit Palais)'. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. Read the Petit Palais record (author, date, PPP2100, dimensions) and the Commons extmetadata; image 3540x4361 px (0.81) matches 81/101 cm (0.80). The spelling 'Paul Cézanne' matches the catalogue's other Cézanne records.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Holbein_Danse_Macab: Commons file page File:Holbein_Danse_Macabre_4.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Holbein_Danse_Macabre_4.jpg) describes it as 'Holbein d. J.; Danse Macabre. IV. The Consequences of the Fall', uses {{Creator:Hans Holbein d. J.}}, and files it under Category:Danse Macabre (Holbein) with sort key 04. English Wikipedia's 'Hans Lützelburger' article states the Dance of Death woodcuts were designed by Hans Holbein the Younger and cut by Lützelburger. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Commons raw wikitext and the Wikipedia article text; the local image is the woodcut of Adam tilling the soil with Death beside him and Eve nursing at left. 'Hans Holbein the Younger' is the spelling the catalogue already uses for his other ~20 works.
_why.collection-of-beauty/The_muscles_of_the_: Wellcome Collection record https://wellcomecollection.org/works/jesm64dw (API work id cepejhhf, Miro image V0007799, iconographic no. 32556i, Sierra b11903934) is titled 'The muscles of the human body, fourth layer, seen from the front. Colour mezzotint by A. E. Gautier d'Agoty after himself, 1773', lists contributor 'Gautier d'Agoty, A. E. (Arnaud Eloy)', lettering 'A. E. G. D. pin. et scul. cum. pri. R.', production [Nancy] : [J. B. H. Leclerc], [1773]. The Commons file carries category 'Arnauld-Éloi Gautier-Dagoty'. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Wellcome catalogue API JSON (identifiers V0007799 and b1190393 match the Commons file's photo number and bibliographic record) and the Commons raw wikitext. The spelling matches the catalogue's own description of this work; no other Gautier d'Agoty works exist in the catalogue.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Albinus,_Tabulae_sc: The plate's own lettering, lower left, reads 'J. Wandelaar ad ipsa corpora humana delineavit idemque incidit' (drew it from the human bodies themselves and also engraved it); running head 'B. S. ALBINI … MUSCULORUM TABULA II'. Wellcome Collection's record for a Gautier d'Agoty copy of these plates (https://wellcomecollection.org/works/jesm64dw) states the Albinus Tabulae plates were 'drawn and engraved by Jan Wandelaar (1690-1759)'. The book record https://wellcomecollection.org/works/nufbvr6n (API id a43g5vnz) lists Miro image L0023549 among its identifiers. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I zoomed the local image and read the lettering, read the Wellcome API JSON for both records, and confirmed the catalogue already names the artist 'Jan Wandelaar' on Albinus_skeleton_w_muscles.jpg and Albinus_skeleton_w_less_muscles.jpg.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Amor_Vincet_Omnia.j: Commons File:Amor Vincet Omnia.jpg uses {{art photo|wikidata=Q474024}} with provenance commissioned 1601–1602 by Vincenzo Giustiniani, bought 1815 by the Berlin museums; its description reads 'Amor Vincit Omnia (c. 1601–1602), by Caravaggio. Oil on canvas, 156 cm × 113 cm … Gemäldegalerie, Berlin'. Wikidata Q474024 ('Amor Vincit Omnia', painting by Caravaggio) has P170 Q42207 (Caravaggio), P217 inventory 369 in Gemäldegalerie Berlin, 156.5 x 113.3 cm. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Commons raw wikitext and the Wikidata JSON; local image aspect 730x1024 (0.71) matches 113.3x156.5 cm (0.72). The catalogue spells this painter 'Caravaggio' on 15 other works.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Fourth_muscle_man,_: Commons title 'Fourth muscle man, by Vesalius.' with keywords 'Anatomy; Vesalius'; the Wellcome record https://wellcomecollection.org/works/jq3wthjj is Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, Basel, Oporinus, 1555. The woodblock cutters are unrecorded, and the catalogue credits the four other Fabrica plates (De_humani_corporis_fabrica_(24)–(27).jpg) to 'Andreas Vesalius'. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Commons raw wikitext and the Wellcome API JSON, and checked src/data/artworks.json for the 'Andreas Vesalius' precedent (4 works).
_why.collection-of-beauty/Holbein_Danse_Macab: Commons raw wikitext for File:Holbein_Danse_Macabre_34.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=File%3AHolbein_Danse_Macabre_34.jpg&action=raw) reads 'Holbein d. J.; Danse Macabre. XXXIV. The Countess' with {{Creator:Hans Holbein d. J.}}, category 'Danse Macabre (Holbein)|34', and links Hollar's later etched copies of the Countess as other versions. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the raw wikitext; the local image is the woodcut of Death helping a young woman dress while a maid hands her a chain, with an hourglass on the chest (the Countess plate). scripts/artists-db.json names him 'Hans Holbein the Younger' with alias 'Hans Holbein d. J.', used on 23 catalogue works; the bare name is correct, the '(designer)' suffix is not used elsewhere.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Jan_van_der_Hoecke_: Royal Collection Trust lists RCIN 400100 as 'Jan van der Hoecke (Antwerp 1611 - Antwerp or Brussels 1651) - The Battle of Nördlingen, 1634', oil on canvas, 242.0 x 339.6 cm, Windsor Castle (https://www.rct.uk/collection/400100/the-battle-of-nordlingen-1634). Wikidata Q28028894 (P217 'RCIN 400100', P195 Royal Collection Q1459037, P18 = this exact file) gives creators Jan van den Hoecke (Q1349676), Jacob Jordaens (Q270658) and Peter Paul Rubens (Q5599) with Rubens qualified 'applies to part: design' (Q82604). Commons file is categorised 'History paintings by Jan van den Hoecke'. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Wikidata JSON and Commons wikitext directly; rct.uk blocks automated fetches, so the RCT attribution line and 242.0 x 339.6 cm were read from the RCT result title and search extract. Rubens is credited only for the design, so a flat Rubens attribution is wrong; the RCT spelling 'van der Hoecke' matches the file name and the record's own description (no artists-db entry exists for either spelling).
_why.collection-of-beauty/Jean_Frédéric_Bazil: Commons raw wikitext for File:Jean_Frédéric_Bazille_-_Reclining_Nude_-_1864.jpg gives author {{Creator:Frédéric Bazille}}, date 1864, 70.5 x 190.5 cm, Musée Fabre, Montpellier, category 'Paintings by Frédéric Bazille in the Musée Fabre', wikidata Q95691951. Wikidata Q95691951 ('Reclining Nude', P18 = this file) has creator Frédéric Bazille (Q207298), inception 1864, collection Musée Fabre (Q1519002), inventory 18.1.1. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Commons wikitext and Wikidata JSON; the catalogue spells him 'Frédéric Bazille' on 21 other works.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Plate_from_Le_Brun,: Wellcome Collection catalogue record for image L0012148 (https://wellcomecollection.org/works/qtnm6psg, resolving to work m67r982x; ESTC T220787) names the book 'Bowles's Passions of the soul / represented in several heads; engraved in the manner of drawings in chalk, from the designs of ... M. le Brun.', published 'London : C. Bowles, [1785?]'. It lists Charles Le Brun as primary contributor. The Commons file (Wellcome L0012148, keywords 'Physiognomy; Charles Le Brun') cites that record. The proposed string 'after Charles Le Brun, printed for Carington Bowles' is amended to 'Charles Le Brun', because an artist override is looked up by name in scripts/artists-db.json. The free-text form would create a new one-work artist page. The sibling plates from the same Wellcome series (horror-from-le-brun-wellcome-l0012156, simple-bodily-pain-from-le-brun-wellcome-l0012151) are already catalogued under 'Charles Le Brun'. Bowles was the publisher, not the artist, and the engraver is unnamed. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED. I read the Wellcome catalogue API record (title, production, contributors) and the Commons raw wikitext.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Thomas_Gainsborough: Yale Center for British Art B1977.14.6174, Paul Mellon Collection. Its IIIF manifest (https://manifests.collections.yale.edu/ycba/obj/9916) is labelled 'imitator of Thomas Gainsborough, 1727–1788, Cattle Watering by a Stream, undated'; medium 'Watercolor and gouache with black chalk over graphite on medium, slightly textured, cream laid paper', sheet 29.5 x 36.2 cm. The collection page (https://collections.britishart.yale.edu/catalog/tms:9916) gives the same attribution. The name 'Thomas Gainsborough' reached the catalogue from the Google Art Project file on Commons. Recorded as 'Imitator of Thomas Gainsborough', following the one precedent in the catalogue ('Follower of Rogier van der Weyden'): the qualified name is its own artist, so the work leaves Gainsborough's artist page and count, and it matches no artists-db entry. Found during the September 2026 physical-size fixes (metadata/real-size-fixes-2026-09.md).
_why.collection-of-beauty/Amalia_van_Solms_(G: Rijksmuseum SK-A-179, on loan to Huygens' Hofwijck, Voorburg. The museum's Linked Art record (https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200109387, found through https://data.rijksmuseum.nl/search/collection?objectNumber=SK-A-179) gives the maker as 'painter: workshop of Gerard van Honthorst'; 1650, oil on canvas, 125.2 x 102.2 cm, signed 'GHonthorst / 1650'. Wikidata Q17319888 agrees (P170 unknown value, qualified 'workshop of' Honthorst). The alias matcher read Honthorst out of the sidecar string 'Workshop of Gerard van Honthorst'. Recorded with the Rijksmuseum's qualifier, so the portrait leaves Honthorst's artist page. It is the pendant of SK-A-178, Frederik Hendrik, which has the same attribution. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Frederik_Hendrik_(1: Rijksmuseum SK-A-178, on loan to Huygens' Hofwijck, Voorburg. The museum's Linked Art record (https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200109386, found through data.rijksmuseum.nl by object number) gives the maker as 'painter: workshop of Gerard van Honthorst'; 1650, oil on canvas, 125 x 102 cm, signed 'GHonthorst 1650'. Wikidata Q17319887 still gives plain Honthorst, behind the museum. The alias matcher read Honthorst out of the sidecar string 'Workshop of Gerard van Honthorst'. Recorded with the Rijksmuseum's qualifier, so the portrait leaves Honthorst's artist page. Pendant of SK-A-179, Amalia van Solms. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Hieronymous Bosch T: Museo Lázaro Galdiano, Madrid, inv. 02892. The museum's record (https://www.museolazarogaldiano.es/fondos/vision-de-tondal) gives 'Hieronymus van Aeken (El Bosco): Taller de' and concludes, after López Redondo (2017, 2023), that the panel is attributable to the painter's workshop; 1491-1525, fatty tempera on oak, 54 x 72 cm. Commons (File:Follower_of_Jheronimus_Bosch_037.jpg) still has the older 'follower of' reading, and Wikidata Q14942621 gives plain Bosch. The alias matcher read Bosch out of the sidecar string 'Follower of Hieronymus Bosch'. Recorded as the museum's current attribution, so the panel leaves Bosch's artist page. The catalogue's mid-16th-century date comes from Commons and disagrees with the museum; it is not changed here. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Ingres_(atelier)_-_: La Piscine, Roubaix, inv. 11747-155-141, Henri Selosse bequest, 1923. The museum's navigart collection database (https://api.navigart.fr/23/artworks?q=Angélique) gives 'Jean-Auguste-Dominique INGRES (atelier de)', title 'Angélique', '1er quart XIXe siècle?', oil on canvas, 102 x 73.7 cm. Wikidata Q62035061 agrees (P170 unknown value, qualified 'workshop of' Ingres). The alias matcher read Ingres out of the sidecar string 'Workshop of Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres', and the sidecar's artist_info snapshot named Ingres too. Recorded with the museum's qualifier, so the canvas leaves Ingres's artist page. The workshop has no artists-db entry; metadata/movement-overrides.json tags it Neoclassicism so it keeps its floor. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
Private collection; no museum holds it. Stockholms Auktionsverk sold it on 7 December 2021 (lot 345, auctionet 1975793) as 'LUCAS CRANACH THE ELDER. ATELIER.', with a letter from Dieter Koepplin (2 December 2021) calling it a work from the elder Cranach's workshop; c. 1525-1530, oil on panel, 22 x 46 cm. The Cranach Digital Archive (https://lucascranach.org/de/PRIVATE_NONE-P368) gives 'Werkstatt Lucas Cranach der Ältere', 'nach 1530'. Commons and Wikidata Q116962838 both say 'workshop of'. The alias matcher read Cranach out of the sidecar string 'Workshop of Lucas Cranach the Elder'. Recorded with the qualifier, so the panel leaves Cranach's artist page. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Mann_mit_dem_Goldhe: Gemäldegalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, inv. 811A, owned by the Kaiser Friedrich-Museums-Verein. The SMB record (https://id.smb.museum/object/865524) gives 'Ausführung: Unbekannt' and 'Umkreis: Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn (1606 - 1669)': an unknown painter of Rembrandt's circle; 1650/60, canvas, 67.5 x 50.7 cm. Its text dates the final de-attribution to 1986. Wikidata Q1195610 agrees (P170 unknown value, 'circle of' Rembrandt; the plain Rembrandt statement is deprecated). The alias matcher read Rembrandt out of the sidecar string 'Circle of Rembrandt'. Recorded with the painter's name spelled as artists-db spells it, as the other qualified names are, so the picture leaves Rembrandt's artist page. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Pallas_Athena_by_Re: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, Lisbon, inv. 1488. The museum's page (https://gulbenkian.pt/museu/en/works/pallas-athena/) gives 'Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn e aluno' (and pupil) and says the picture was made by Rembrandt and a pupil; c. 1657, oil on canvas, 118 x 91 cm. RKD (https://data.rkd.nl/images/54618) gives 'toegeschreven aan Rembrandt en atelier van Rembrandt of atelier van Rembrandt' (attributed to Rembrandt and studio, or studio), citing Corpus vol. 6 (2015), no. 253. The sidecar has 'Attributed to Rembrandt'. Kept under Rembrandt: the museum names him as the principal painter, and the catalogue files 'X and workshop' works under X. Recorded so the decision is on file; the alias matcher already reached the same name. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Descent_from_the_Cr: State Hermitage Museum, inv. ГЭ-753. The Hermitage record (https://hermitagemuseum.org/digital-collection/43510?lng=en) gives 'Author: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669)'; 1634, oil on canvas, 158 x 117 cm. The sidecar's 'Workshop of Rembrandt' follows the Rembrandt Research Project's 1986 opinion (Corpus C 49); RKD (https://data.rkd.nl/images/40838) records that Ernst van de Wetering returned the work to Rembrandt in Corpus vol. 6 (2015), no. 126. Kept under Rembrandt, as the holding museum catalogues it. Recorded because the alias matcher no longer reads Rembrandt out of 'Workshop of Rembrandt', so without this entry the work would leave his page. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/After_Benjamin_West: National Gallery of Art, Washington, 1942.8.39, Andrew W. Mellon Collection. The NGA page (https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1133-benjamin-west) gives 'after Benjamin West' and lists 'Unknown 18th Century, Painter' and 'Benjamin West, Artist After'; c. 1776, oil on canvas, 75.8 x 63 cm. Exhibitions up to 1950 and the NGA's own catalogue of 1992 gave it as a self-portrait by West. Wikidata Q20178792 agrees (P170 unknown value, anonymous). The alias matcher read West out of the sidecar string 'After Benjamin West'. Recorded as the NGA gives it, so the copy leaves West's artist page. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/After_Rubens_-_Anne: Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, INV 1794 (MR 984). The Louvre record (https://collections.louvre.fr/ark:/53355/cl010060852) gives 'Rubens, Petrus Paulus, D'après' and 'Pays-Bas du Sud, École de'; 1620/1625, oil on wood, 1.05 x 0.93 m. Its note calls the picture not a workshop replica but a rather heavy old copy ('Non pas réplique d'atelier, mais assez lourde copie ancienne'); the original is lost. The alias matcher read Rubens out of the sidecar string 'After Peter Paul Rubens'. Recorded as the Louvre gives it, so the copy leaves Rubens's artist page. Independently re-checked: VERIFIED against the sources cited, September 2026.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Arcimboldo_Air_(cop: Private collection, Switzerland, per Commons; no museum record exists. Commons gives {{Creator:Giuseppe Arcimboldo}} with the 'after' qualifier and cites the Kunsthistorisches Museum's 2008 exhibition catalogue, p. 147 (not read here); oil on canvas, 74.4 x 56 cm.
